feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 6 (score 658) is the best measured design: body_length 0.10, mass 0.6, sensors y 0.07, 12 mm footprint, wheel_track 0.09. It gave the s-bend 19 of 20 finishes with line losses 0.55 and oscillation 0.33, and the oval 20 of 20 with max_error 0.017. Iteration 7 (mass 0.5) reversed that gain: s-bend fell to 18 finishes, losses rose to 0.85, and progress fell to 0.965. Mass 0.6 is therefore the floor, and body_length 0.10 is at its minimum. The slalom has been at its max_error floor (0.063) with 0 finishes in every iteration, and it has not responded to any inertia change. Iteration 2 (y 0.07, wheel_track 0.10) gave the best slalom line-loss count so far (1.0), which is why look-ahead is the next test. Read the next race as follows. If the s-bend holds 19 or more finishes with line losses at or below 0.55, and the oval max_error stays near 0.017 to 0.025, keep y 0.075. If the oval max_error rises above about 0.025 or s-bend oscillation rises above about 0.35, the extra look-ahead is adding lag, so return to y 0.07. If the slalom is still at its max_error floor with 0 finishes after y 0.075, geometry is near its limit and the next step should be a controller change.
requested_changes: Keep mass 0.6 and body_length 0.10 (do not go to mass 0.5). Iteration 7 showed mass 0.5 cut s-bend finishes from 19 to 18 and raised line losses from 0.55 to 0.85.

If slalom line losses stay near or above 1.1 with progress at 0.26 after y 0.075, try wheel_track 0.095 as a compromise. Iteration 2 (track 0.10, y 0.07) gave slalom losses 1.0, while iteration 3 (track 0.09) gave 1.85 and s-bend progress 0.68. This trades s-bend progress against slalom retention.

If the oval max_error rises above about 0.025 at y 0.075, return to y 0.07, since iteration 6 gave oval max_error 0.017 and y 0.07 is the last layout where the oval clearly held margin. If the slalom is still at its max_error floor with 0 finishes at either y, stop changing geometry and test a controller gain change (kd 0.6 or kp 2.5).
